title: Thrift binary protocol
summary: Apache Thrift's binary protocol encodes each field as: 1-byte type, 2-byte field ID (big-endian), then the value. A struct is a sequence of fields terminated by a STOP (type 0). Types: 0 STOP, 1 VOID, 2 BOOL, 3 BYTE, 4 I16, 5 I32, 6 I64, 7 DOUBLE, 8 STRING (4-byte length + bytes), 9 MAP, 10 SET, 11 LIST, 12 STRUCT, 13 UUID (16 bytes).

notes: Thrift supports multiple protocols: binary (default), compact (zigzag + varint, smaller), JSON, and simple JSON.
Thrift includes an IDL (Interface Definition Language) and code generators for 20+ languages.
Thrift is used by Facebook, Twitter, Uber, and many microservice architectures.
The compact protocol uses zigzag encoding and varints for smaller payloads.
